column2: Patient & relative identifiers: name, phone, e-mail, address, IP
column3: Not needed to assess urgency; relatives' data is third-party data
column4: GDPR Art. 4(1), 5(1)(c), 25, 32; Recital 30; CJEU C-582/14 Breyer
column6: Agent replaces every variant with case tokens BEFORE BRANE ([FIRST_n] [LAST_n], titles kept so relatives stay distinguishable); BRANE PERSON/EMAIL/PHONE/ADDRESS/IP_ADDRESS = local
column7: BRANE alone missed name variants on cloud turns ('J. Beispiel', bare first names) and tags words like 'Mark', 'Hello', 'Scrum' as PERSON. Wish: entity linking of name variants, and a per-category 'strip from prompt' action
column8: Agent log 'Text handed to BRANE' has no names; X-Brane-Routed-To: local

column2: Date of birth
column3: Age can matter clinically; the full date does not
column6: Agent converts DOB to age ([AGE_1: 68 years]) before BRANE; BRANE DATE_OF_BIRTH = local
column7: BRANE can mask or route a DOB but not generalise it to an age; wish: 'generalise' action
column8: Text handed to BRANE shows age, not date

column2: National ID, passport, tax, insurance, hospital record / encounter numbers
column3: Not needed for triage; identity matching stays in the clinical system
column6: Agent replaces IDs with case tokens; BRANE SSN/PASSPORT/TAX_NUMBER/INSURANCE_NUMBER/ACCOUNT_NUMBER = local; re-identification map kept in memory only
column7: BRANE tags hospital record numbers (MRN) as ACCOUNT_NUMBER, so a financial category has to be treated as a patient identifier

column2: Organisation names, trade register, VAT
column3: Hospital / provider names in patient material may be confidential
column4: GDPR Art. 4(1), 5, 32
column6: BRANE ORG/TRADE_REGISTER/VAT_ID = local
column7: One rule per category: cannot allow a public company lookup in one sub-step and keep it local in another

column2: Payment data: IBAN, credit card
column3: Irrelevant to clinical triage
column4: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 32 (PCI DSS is an industry standard, not EU law)
column6: Agent deletes the value before BRANE ('[removed: not needed for triage]'), case continues; BRANE IBAN/CREDIT_CARD = refuse as safety net
column7: BRANE 'refuse' stops the whole request; there is no 'remove from prompt' action, so removal is done locally

column2: Credentials: passwords, API keys
column3: Never needed; security incident if exposed
column4: GDPR Art. 32; NIS2 Art. 20-21 where applicable
column6: BRANE PASSWORD/SECRET_KEY = refuse

column2: Health data of an identifiable patient: symptoms, vitals, medication, allergies, history, pregnancy, disability, mental health, indirect health context
column3: Needed for the triage suggestion, must not leave the hospital
column4: GDPR Art. 5, 6, 9(1), 9(2)(h), 9(3), 25, 32, 35; CJEU C-21/23 Lindenapotheke; EU AI Act Annex III 5(d)
column6: BRANE HEALTH_DATA = local + semantic PATIENT_CLINICAL_CONTEXT = local (incl. first-person symptoms); model 'auto' so BRANE routes to the internal GPU
column7: HEALTH_DATA alone cannot tell general medical knowledge from patient data, and built-in detection varied between runs; the semantic category is the stable rule

column2: Ethnicity, religion, political opinion, sexual orientation, trade union
column3: Never a triage-ranking feature
column4: GDPR Art. 5, 9(1), 22; CJEU C-184/20 OT; EU Charter Art. 7, 8, 21; ECHR Art. 8, 9
column6: BRANE categories = local; agent hides the label before BRANE ([RELIGIOUS_BELIEF_1]); system prompt forbids using traits for urgency
column7: BRANE cannot separate 'religious label' from 'treatment preference'; done locally
column8: Label token in payload; semantic matches

column2: Specific treatment refusal or advance directive (e.g. no blood transfusion)
column3: Clinically essential, must reach the clinician as the specific preference
column4: GDPR Art. 9(1), 9(3); ECHR Art. 8; Oviedo Convention Art. 9; ECtHR Pindo Mulla v Spain (15541/20), Jehovah's Witnesses of Moscow v Russia (302/02)
column6: Semantic TREATMENT_REFUSAL_OR_ADVANCE_DIRECTIVE = local; preference text kept, religious label hidden; clinician verifies wishes and capacity

column2: Requests to decide capacity or who may consent for the patient
column3: Legal capacity and representation are assessed by clinicians under national law
column4: GDPR Art. 5, 9; Oviedo Convention Art. 5, 6; ECHR Art. 8
column6: Agent refuses before any model call; semantic CAPACITY_OR_CONSENT_DETERMINATION = refuse (422)

column2: Requests to rank or delay a patient by origin, religion, language, disability
column3: Urgency may only depend on clinical findings
column4: GDPR Art. 9(1), 22; EU Charter Art. 21, 35; UN CRPD Art. 25
column6: Agent refuses; semantic PROTECTED_TRAIT_PRIORITISATION = refuse (422); system prompt forbids trait-based urgency

column2: Emotion, personality or honesty inference
column3: Not needed for triage; high legal and safety risk
column4: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f), Annex III; GDPR Art. 9
column6: Agent refuses; semantic EMOTION_OR_BIOMETRIC_INFERENCE = refuse

column2: Police custody / criminal context
column3: Not needed to treat the injury
column4: GDPR Art. 10
column6: Semantic CUSTODY_OR_CRIMINAL_CONTEXT = local
column7: No built-in category for Art. 10 data

column2: Patient identifiable from context without a name
column3: Context is re-identifying
column4: GDPR Art. 4(1), Recital 26; CJEU C-582/14 Breyer
column6: Semantic CONTEXT_IDENTIFIABLE_PATIENT = local
column7: Regex/NER cannot see this; relies on the semantic model

column2: Instructions embedded in case text (prompt injection)
column3: Patient text is data, never commands
column4: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f), 25, 32; EU AI Act Art. 15
column6: Agent quarantines instruction sentences before BRANE; masking does not depend on detecting the injection; BRANE injection detector as second layer
column7: BRANE flags injection but cannot remove only the injected sentence

column2: Autonomous refusal, discharge, delay or deprioritisation
column3: Only a clinician may take consequential action
column4: GDPR Art. 22; EU AI Act Art. 14, 26, Annex III 5(d); CJEU C-634/21 SCHUFA
column6: Agent refuses before any model call; semantic AUTONOMOUS_CLINICAL_DECISION = refuse (422)
column7: BRANE scans our own system prompt as data: our wording first triggered this rule and had to be rephrased

column2: Triage recommendation / urgency level (HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP)
column3: AI output is decision support only
column4: GDPR Art. 22; EU AI Act Art. 14, 26; CJEU C-634/21 SCHUFA
column6: Nurse must pick the category herself (nothing preselected); if she differs from the AI a reason is required; final_category, ai_suggested and overrode_ai are logged

column2: Logs, prompts, outputs
column3: Accountability without storing patient data
column6: Audit log stores hashes, labels and X-Brane headers only; 30-day retention enforced at start-up
column7: This demo's BRANE is hosted by AI-Z and receives the raw case text for inspection; provider-side retention is not verified (production: on-premise BRANE)

column2: BRANE inspection failure, timeout or outage
column3: No uninspected transfer
column4: GDPR Art. 25, 32; EU AI Act Art. 15
column6: Single network path; any error -> stop, nothing sent, manual clinical fallback

column2: General clinical knowledge with no patient (protocol questions)
column3: No data subject; cloud model gives better answers
column4: GDPR Art. 4(1), Recital 26
column6: No category triggered -> cloud
